messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — high OOM rate observed on runtime pool rt-prod-3. 58% failure rate (OOM) in last 5m. Paging: @dave_oncall @alice_runtime @bob_sre @carol_support :rotating_light:

_dave_oncall:_ On it. Pulling up metrics and checking routing.

_alice_runtime:_ I see a correlation: spiky arrival rate + sustained large batch sizes on route /chat/stream -> KV cache size grows, fragmentation shows on memory heatmaps. Hypothesis H1: KV cache growth + large batch -> fragmentation + pinned allocations.

_bob_sre:_ Can you paste GPU mem and process maps? Also need nvidia-smi and dmesg around OOMs.

_alice_runtime:_ adding quick dumps from the 2 affected hosts (rt-3b, rt-3c) — last 30s around the spike:

```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0
GPU 0:
  FB Memory Usage
    Total                      : 32510 MiB
    Used                       : 31442 MiB
    Free                       : 1068 MiB

# processes (rt-3b)
PID   GPU_MEM
10234 12000 MiB  redwood-runtime-worker
10245 9000 MiB   redwood-runtime-worker
10256 4000 MiB   redwood-runtime-worker
10267 3500 MiB   redwood-runtime-worker
# note: fragmentation metric: free contiguous chunk ~600 MiB
```
\n```
# dmesg tail around OOM
[ 142420.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 10234 (redwood-runtime) total-vm: 512000kB, anon-rss: 200000kB, file-rss: 0kB
[ 142420.123460] GPU driver: attempted allocation failed: insufficient contiguous memory
```
\n_carol_support:_ Customer A reported multiple 500s in the same window — raising priority and emailing their on-call.

_dave_oncall:_ Live mitigation proposal: 1) set batch_size=1 on rt-prod-3 routes (reduce transient peak allocations) 2) disable KV cache for the most-used model variant on these routes (kv cache eviction race suspected) 3) spin up 2 nodes in fallback pool and route 20% traffic there as canary. Will roll sequentially.

_eng-runtime-bot:_ Deploy action started: route config change -> batch_size=1, kv_cache=off for route /chat/stream. Rolling to nodes rt-3a,b,c; canary 20% enabled. (deploy id: dep-20260315-01)

_alice_runtime:_ Recording hypotheses (inline):
H1: KV cache growth leads to fragmentation, large batches exacerbate -> OOMs on allocation attempts
H2: Specific worker process leaking pinned GPU memory across inference runs (less likely given multiple PIDs)
H3: Driver-level allocation failure due to lack of contiguous block though total free appears non-zero

_bob_sre:_ Good. While rolling, please capture per-process GPU allocations and run the allocator debug dump on one node:
```
# debug commands to run on affected host
sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime-worker@10234
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-allocator-dump --pid 10234 --out /tmp/alloc-dump-10234.json
```
\n_alice_runtime:_ Ran the allocator dump on rt-3b (attached snippet): shows many small pinned allocations from KV cache and some large cached tensors. Free contiguous biggest chunk reported ~560MB.

_dave_oncall:_ Early results: after batch_size change and kv cache off, overall OOMs dropped from 58% -> 12% in 4 minutes. However, node rt-3b still hits intermittent OOMs ~every 2–3 min. Suspect fragmentation on that GPU.

_alice_runtime:_ Pmap snapshot from the problematic worker on rt-3b before restart:
```
# pmap-like gpu view (simplified)
region_start region_size type
0x70000000  1024MiB   tensor_cache
0x74000000  128MiB    kv_cache_chunk
0x74800000  64MiB     small_pinned
0x75000000  2048MiB   model_weights
0x7d000000  560MiB    free_contiguous
0x7f000000  128MiB    scratch
```

_bob_sre:_ OK. Next live step: restart the runtime worker processes on rt-3b (graceful), set KV_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=128MB and enable aggressive eviction (KV_EVICT_AGGRESSIVE=1). Also keep batch_size=1 until we confirm stability.

_eng-runtime-bot:_ Restart job queued: restart-workers rt-3b -> 8 processes, env update KV_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=128MB, KV_EVICT_AGGRESSIVE=1. (job id: restart-rt3b-20260315-01)

_dave_oncall:_ Executed restart. Monitoring logs.

_alice_runtime:_ Post-restart observation: free contiguous chunks consolidated to ~1.8GiB, OOMs for rt-prod-3 drop to <1% across the pool for 12m. Rolling back kv_cache change? I recommend keeping KV_CACHE at reduced size + eviction for 24h while we run load tests.

_carol_support:_ Customer A status: errors reduced to single-digit requests, they acknowledged workaround and will re-open if they see regressions. :thumbsup:

_bob_sre:_ I'll aggregate logs and draft incident RCA. Key artifacts to attach: allocator dumps, nvidia-smi timeline, dmesg, route config diff, canary traffic graphs. Also recommend we run a reproduction with synthetic big-batch traffic to validate fragmentation.

_dave_oncall:_ Agree. Handoff to next on-call @eve_oncall in 30m. Summary for handoff: P1 rt-prod-3 GPU OOMs caused by fragmentation due to KV cache growth + high batch sizes. Mitigations applied: batch_size=1, kv_cache disabled then resized + aggressive eviction, restarted workers on rt-3b, spun up fallback nodes. Current status: stable with OOMs <1% last 12m.

_eve_oncall:_ Taking over. I have the restart logs and allocator dumps. I'll follow up with a post-incident task: run long-run memdefrag test and add runtime metric alert for contiguous-chunk-size <800MB.

_bob_sre:_ tagging follow-ups for RCA: writeup owner = bob_sre, timeline + artifacts to /docs/incidents/1812345678-rt-prod-3-oom-rca.md, postmortem due EOD tomorrow.

_dave_oncall:_ Thanks team. Closing paging loop. :white_check_mark:
